u05-rem-mid.resolution: I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. 'God swears by himself, since he has no one greater by whom to swear, as Paul says' renders fragment 152's Καθ' ἑαυτοῦ ὄμνυσι θεός, ἐπεὶ κατ' οὐδενὸς ἔχει μείζονος ὀμόσαι, καθάπερ ὁ Παῦλός φησιν, which is in the Greek. The 'invented' flag compared it with the following clause. Ὤμοσα … ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ μου is LXX Ps 88:36 (ἅπαξ ὤμοσα ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ μου), English 89:35; 'Ps 88,39-46' is the next fragment's lemma. Romans 9:6 correctly identifies Paul's Οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι ἐκπέπτωκεν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ, which the Greek attributes to Paul. 2 Chronicles 20:24 and Exodus 23:22 correctly identify the quotations. The rest (ἐπιζητεῖν as 'he seeks', προσθῆναι φθορᾷ 'be handed over to corruption', particles, supplied subjects) is idiom with the same sense.
